lines.text: IT Department progress update, for the thirteenth of October, twenty twenty-six.
This month we tracked ten pieces of work.
Four are completed, three are in progress, and three are planned.
The highlights: WMS now runs on the Azure cloud, Watch Dog covers every SSG car park, and the new season portal is seventy-two percent done.
First, WMS. We took over the project at the start of August.
In three months, it was tested, moved to the cloud, and started its first round of improvements.
User end testing ran from the ninth to the seventeenth of August, and passed.
By the twenty-fourth of August, the development team and the Azure cloud were ready.
The WMS users asked us to migrate from the twenty-second to the twenty-fourth of September, to fit their operations.
WMS moved to the Azure cloud on schedule, and the mobile app upgraded itself automatically.
Then came change request phase one: five improvements asked for by the business.
Ad-hoc collections can be added to a route, and show up within fifteen minutes.
A missed collection can be added later, and is saved against its original date.
Average weight uses the latest seven valid collections, and the formula is shown.
A collection near a shift boundary keeps its planned shift, and records the actual one.
And the daily collection report and dashboard gain new fields, new filters, and matching totals.
The development team ran twenty-four test cases, and all of them passed.
User testing of phase one was planned for the first week of October; at the users' request, it now starts on the twelfth.
Once they confirm, phase one goes live on the production Azure server, and phase two can begin.

Also completed this month: the Central Reports server, for the car parks under Re Sustainability Solutions; the QMS enhancement; and the old season portal, moved to the Re Parking site and rebranded from Times twenty-four to Re twenty-four Parking.
The new season portal, built in-house and still in development, is seventy-two percent complete, on average.
Testing started on the first of October and is half done; it goes live on the first of November.
Its basic functions are done, and the invoice format is confirmed.
The DBS payment gateway is at eighty percent, season sync at seventy, the various reports at fifty, and the credit and sale note upload to Nav at thirty.
When it goes live, invoices and payment reminders will look like this, with a PayNow code to scan.
Watch Dog monitoring is live at every SSG car park, and the rollout at Ehub has started, at ten percent.
On the O-P-Cs, UltraVNC will replace RealVNC, which needs a licence.
And at Ehub, we will uninstall Carbon Black, an unlicensed tool left by the previous IT team.
Next: start user testing on the twelfth and deploy phase one, finish the payment gateway and season sync, and continue the Ehub rollout.
Then switch to UltraVNC, and remove Carbon Black.
Thank you.
